name: Priscilla and Aquila
charge: Laying down their own necks for Paul’s life; and expounding unto Apollos the way of God more perfectly
summary: Paul found at Corinth a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome, and because he was of the same craft he abode with them and wrought. They sailed with him to Ephesus and stayed there, and when Apollos came speaking only of the baptism of John, they took him and expounded the way of God more perfectly. Paul afterward called them his helpers in Christ Jesus, who had laid down their own necks for his life, and said that all the churches of the Gentiles gave them thanks.
offenseFull: After Athens, Paul came to Corinth and found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome (Acts 18:1-2). Claudius was the Roman emperor from the year forty-one to fifty-four, and the histories date that expulsion around the year forty-nine, which is why the two of them had just arrived. Aquila was born in Pontus, which is in Asia Minor, in what is Turkey today, and he had been living in Italy, which is nothing strange, because our people were scattered through Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia, and into Rome itself, as the list of dwellers at Jerusalem shows (Acts 2:9-10). Scholars cannot tell a Roman Jew from a Roman by his name alone for the same reason.

Because Paul was of the same craft he abode with them and wrought, for by their occupation they were tentmakers (Acts 18:3). They were already believers, holding the same thing he held, which is why he lodged with them and not merely near them. The household and the trade became part of the ministry; he lived and worked in their house while he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath and persuaded the Jews and the Greeks, the southern kingdom and the northern (Acts 18:4). When he departed he took them with him and sailed to Syria, and left them at Ephesus while he went into the synagogue there and reasoned with the Jews (Acts 18:18-19). They stayed where they had been set.

At Ephesus a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man and mighty in the scriptures, began to speak boldly in the synagogue, knowing only the baptism of John; and when Aquila and Priscilla had heard him, they took him to themselves and expounded the way of God to him more perfectly (Acts 18:24-26). They did not contend with him publicly and they did not leave him where he was. A tentmaker and his wife carried what he lacked to him privately.
judgmentFull: When Apollos was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him, and when he was come he helped them much which had believed through grace, for he mightily convinced the Jews, and that publicly, showing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ (Acts 18:27-28). What they gave him in a house at Ephesus went on working in another province.

Paul afterward greeted Priscilla and Aquila as his helpers in Christ Jesus, who had for his life laid down their own necks, to whom not only he gave thanks but also all the churches of the Gentiles, and greeted the church that was in their house (Romans 16:3-5). He sent their salutation again from Ephesus with the church that was in their house (1 Corinthians 16:19), and named them once more at the very end of his last letter (2 Timothy 4:19). Their work, their lodging, their teaching, and their risk are all in the record, and the thanks the churches owed them was not a private friendship but a debt many congregations owed.

taught.title: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

text.text: After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth;
And found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:) and came unto them.
Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and the dwellers in Mesopotamia, and in Judea, and Cappadocia, in Pontus, and Asia,
Phrygia, and Pamphylia, in Egypt, and in the parts of Libya about Cyrene, and strangers of Rome, Jews and proselytes,
And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.
And he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded the Jews and the Greeks.

And Paul after this tarried there yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow.
And he came to Ephesus, and left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.
And a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus.
This man was instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in the spirit, he spake and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.
And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.
And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him: who, when he was come, helped them much which had believed through grace:
For he mightily convinced the Jews, and that publickly, shewing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ.
Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus:
Who have for my life laid down their own necks: unto whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles.
Likewise greet the church that is in their house. Salute my wellbeloved Epenetus, who is the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ.
The churches of Asia salute you. Aquila and Priscilla salute you much in the Lord, with the church that is in their house.
Salute Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus.
